clue.text: Seabird beginning to get out of breath, apparently

parts.note: the puffin is a seabird with a bright striped bill

indicators.note: the beginning of the word get is its opening letter

explanation.surface: A seabird starting to look breathless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'apparently' marks the definition as a playful one: a bird name plus a letter looks like a breathless word.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone panting hard after effort is said to be huffing and puffing, i.e. short of breath.

clue.text: Quid secures a second nut

indicators.note: the tobacco piece holds the other letters fast inside it

parts.note: a quid is a lump of tobacco for chewing, a chew

explanation.surface: A pound coin buys a second nut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quid' looks like a pound sterling (giving CASH, which misleads); here it is a plug of chewing tobacco.
explanation.definitionFit: A kidney-shaped edible seed from a tropical tree, sold among other nuts.

clue.text: Mean to keep a single one from a large brood in litter

indicators.note: the first word holds the single letter inside it

parts.note: to mean to do something is to plan it
a single one is A
a quin is one of five babies born together

explanation.surface: A runt from a big litter of animals is kept back by someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'litter' looks like a brood of animals, fitting the surface, but it is a carried couch.
explanation.definitionFit: A litter in the old sense is an enclosed seat borne on poles, which is what this Asian conveyance is.

clue.text: Take run from end to start of external path

indicators.note: the run letter is taken up and shifted
the letter at the tail of the word is moved to its front

parts.note: external means outer
R is the cricket abbreviation for a run

explanation.surface: An instruction to run the full length of an outer track.
explanation.definitionFit: A path or way taken from one place to another is a course or road.

clue.text: Poor Tom raged madly

indicators.note: acting madly the letters are wildly jumbled

explanation.surface: A poor fellow called Tom went into a fury.
explanation.walkthrough: In King Lear, Gloucester's son disguises himself as the mad beggar Poor Tom, which makes 'madly' doubly apt.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's King Lear has Gloucester's legitimate son disguise himself as the beggar Poor Tom.

clue.text: Bogus instrument stopping short, the Irish party on

indicators.note: in an across clue, on means placed after
the instrument's name is cut off before its final letter

parts.note: a trumpet is a brass musical instrument
the DUP is the Democratic Unionist Party of Northern Ireland

explanation.surface: A fake musician quits early while an Irish political party plays on.
explanation.definitionFit: Charges that are fabricated or concocted are called false or fake.

clue.text: Unspecified item that I can do better than you in Berlin

definitions.text: that I can do better than you in Berlin
definitions.meaning: in Irving Berlin's song from Annie Get Your Gun, 'whatever you can do, I can do better' begins with this word

explanation.surface: A boast of being better than someone at an unnamed thing in Germany's capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Berlin' looks like the German city; it is Irving Berlin, the songwriter.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means whatever object you like, and it opens the famous Irving Berlin song lyric of rivalry.

clue.text: Paper that reflects one's views?

definitions.meaning: the Daily ... is a British tabloid newspaper
a looking glass reflects whatever looks into it

explanation.surface: A newspaper that echoes its reader's opinions.
explanation.walkthrough: The Daily Mirror is a British tabloid; 'views' plays on opinions and on what one sees.
explanation.definitionFit: A British tabloid newspaper shares its name with a looking glass, which literally reflects what one sees.

clue.text: Make most of young person's cape

parts.note: to do is to make or carry out

indicators.note: the word loses its final letter, leaving most of it

parts.note: a minor is a young person under age

explanation.surface: Getting full value from a youngster's cloak.
explanation.definitionFit: A domino is a loose hooded cloak worn with a half-mask at masquerades.

clue.text: With bribe, mean to grab a place to live

parts.note: a bung is a British slang term for a bribe
mean or base behaviour is low

explanation.surface: A miserly person uses a bribe to secure a home.
explanation.walkthrough: BUNG is British slang for a bribe or backhander.
explanation.definitionFit: A one-storey house is a dwelling, somewhere to live.

clue.text: Agreement best rejected? It may be squeezed

parts.note: an accord is an agreement

indicators.note: rejected means turned back, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: number one, written NO 1, means the best

explanation.surface: A deal is turned down; perhaps pressure will be applied.
explanation.walkthrough: The 1 of NO 1 is read as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: This bellows instrument is played by compressing and expanding it between the hands.

clue.text: What students may acquire, having taken in university, for start of career perhaps

indicators.note: the word for what is owed absorbs the university letter

parts.note: students often run up debt from loans

explanation.surface: Students borrow at university and start careers burdened.
explanation.definitionFit: A first public appearance marks the launch of a performer's working life.

clue.text: Point of name given to Norse deity

indicators.note: the letter for name is handed over and added on

parts.note: Thor is the Norse god of thunder

explanation.surface: Asking the purpose of giving a name to a Norse god.
explanation.definitionFit: A prickle or spike on a rose stem is a sharp point.

clue.text: Swearing needs constant replacing with new, to be original

indicators.note: the constant letter is swapped out and the new letter put in its place

parts.note: invective is abusive, swearing language
C is the standard symbol for a constant (as the speed of light)

explanation.surface: Fresh cursing is needed to be original.
explanation.definitionFit: Inventive work is creative, showing fresh imagination.

clue.text: Estuary English lacking in harsh north

indicators.note: the word for harsh goes without the English letter

parts.note: severe means harsh

explanation.surface: Estuary English, the London accent, without a harsh northern edge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Estuary English' looks like the southeast English accent; 'Estuary' alone is the definition. The Severn is Britain's longest river, with a wide estuary into the Bristol Channel.
explanation.definitionFit: Britain's longest river ends in a broad tidal mouth into the Bristol Channel.

clue.text: Engineers alter small screen

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps
to redo something is to change it

explanation.surface: Engineers modify a little screen, as in a gadget.
explanation.definitionFit: This ornamental partition stands behind a church altar, a kind of decorative screen.

clue.text: Such hair appals — pretend that's fashionable

indicators.note: read as able to be fashioned, the letters can be shaped into a new order

explanation.surface: Greying hair is appalling; pretending it is fashionable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fashionable' looks like a compliment, but it signals that the letters are to be fashioned anew.
explanation.definitionFit: Hair flecked with grey and dark strands is described by comparison with mixed condiments.

clue.text: Patsy, stay beside sink

indicators.note: one word set next to the other

parts.note: to sink is to fall
a guy is a rope that stays or steadies a tent or mast

explanation.surface: A woman named Patsy stays next to the kitchen sink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stay' is a noun here: a supporting rope, as a guy rope on a tent.
explanation.definitionFit: A patsy is a dupe or scapegoat who takes the blame for others.

clue.text: Champion has split from wife in secret

indicators.note: the champion separates from the wife letter, losing it

parts.note: a champion is a winner

explanation.surface: A champion has separated from their wife in private.
explanation.definitionFit: Feelings kept private and hidden from others are called innermost or personal.

clue.text: Shovelling pounds into stomach, man shows this?

definitions.text: Shovelling pounds into stomach, man shows this?

indicators.note: the pounds letter goes inside the stomach

parts.note: the gut is the stomach
L is the abbreviation for pounds (libra)
Tony is a man's name

explanation.surface: A man stuffing his face displays a deadly sin.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and a picture of greed; 'Shovelling' only sets the scene.
explanation.definitionFit: Eating to excess, shovelling food in, is the deadly sin of greed.

clue.text: Agree to play trick on scoundrel

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means placed above

parts.note: to con someone is to play a trick on them
a cur is a contemptible scoundrel

explanation.surface: Agreeing to trick a rogue.
explanation.definitionFit: To share the same opinion as someone is to be of one mind with them.

clue.text: Youth needs one place in train

indicators.note: the letters for one and place go inside the train word

parts.note: a string, as a string of horses, is a train or series
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A young person needs a seat on a train.
explanation.definitionFit: A stripling is a young man not yet fully grown, an adolescent.

clue.text: These days, gold underpinning unit of currency in republic

indicators.note: in a down clue, the later letters sit below the currency and prop it up

parts.note: the ecu was the European Currency Unit before the euro
AD (anno Domini) marks the present era
or is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: Nowadays gold backs a nation's currency.
explanation.definitionFit: This South American country on the equator is a republic.

clue.text: Former head restrains insolent humour, being courted for knowledge

parts.note: ex means former
pert means cheeky, insolent
wit is humour
a ness is a headland, as in Loch Ness or Sheerness

explanation.surface: An old boss holds back cheeky jokes while being wooed for their know-how.
explanation.walkthrough: 'courted' looks like wooed but means called into court.
explanation.definitionFit: A specialist called to give evidence in a trial is summoned to court for their expertise.

clue.text: Deer sprint round back of broken barrier

parts.note: a hind is a female deer

indicators.note: the sprint word goes round the picked letter

parts.note: a sprint is a race

indicators.note: the back of the word broken is its last letter

explanation.surface: A deer dashes round the end of a broken fence.
explanation.definitionFit: An obstacle or impediment is a barrier that holds one back.

clue.text: Pastry case that firm makes

definitions.meaning: a folded pastry with a filling, as an apple pastry
a company's total sales over a period

explanation.surface: Asking what a company produces, reading it as a bakery.
explanation.definitionFit: A folded pastry parcel shares its name with a company's annual sales figure.

clue.text: One spreading disease died in botched crime

indicators.note: the died letters go inside the jumbled word
a crime done badly is botched, so its letters are messed up

parts.note: OB (obiit) is the abbreviation for died

explanation.surface: A disease-spreader dies in a bungled crime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'botched' rearranges the crime letters to MICRE, and the died abbreviation sits inside that, before the final E.
explanation.definitionFit: A germ or bacterium is a tiny organism that carries infection.

clue.text: Solicited, one threw up outside

indicators.note: the throwing word goes outside the one letter

parts.note: to lob is to throw high
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone who was asked threw up outside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'threw up' looks like vomiting; it means tossed high.
explanation.definitionFit: To press politicians to support a cause is to petition or canvass them.

clue.text: Underling working under car

indicators.note: in a down clue, the working word goes beneath the car

parts.note: the Mini is a famous small British car
a machine that is on is working

explanation.surface: A junior employee working beneath a car, as a mechanic.
explanation.walkthrough: The Mini is a classic small British car.
explanation.definitionFit: A servile subordinate or lackey is a lowly underling.

clue.text: Hearing of Alice's cat café

indicators.note: what is heard is the sound of the cat's name, not its spelling

parts.note: Dinah is Alice's cat in Lewis Carroll's Alice in Wonderland

explanation.surface: Hearing of a café run by Alice's cat.
explanation.walkthrough: In non-rhotic British speech the cat's name and the eatery sound alike.
explanation.definitionFit: A diner is a small cheap restaurant, as a roadside café.
